newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Former RBA head Fraser says time to target jobless.
newsitem.headline: Former RBA head Fraser says time to target jobless.

text.p: Former Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Bernie Fraser said on Wednesday it was now time for the central bank to shift its main focus away from controlling inflation towards boosting growth and employment.

"I've come to understand that at times the primary focus of monetary policy has to shift from inflation to other things like growth and employment and I would suggest that now is one of those times," Fraser told a book launch in Sydney.
Fraser ended his seven-year term as governor in mid-September and was succeeded by Ian Macfarlane, who is generally seen as more hawkish towards inflation.

Macfarlane agreed with the government when appointed that the bank's target of keeping underlying inflation within a two to three percent band on average over the economic cycle would be the key determinant of monetary policy.
Fraser said in December last year that he believed the bank should have cut official interest rates faster and further than it did late last year.
His comments then prompted a sharp selloff in the Australian dollar. Treasurer Peter Costello said after Fraser's December comments that Fraser was commenting as a private citizen.
